events.quote: On July 11, 2024, an issue pertaining to a Front Gross Axle Weight Rating (FGAWR) discrepancy on Incomplete Vehicle Labels (IVL) of 2024 Ford Transit vehicles was brought to Ford’s Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG).

The investigation determined that due to an oversight during Ford’s label review process, incomplete 2024 Transit cut-away vehicles equipped with 1,875kg FGAWR axles, 3.5L twin independent variable cam timing engines, single rear wheels, rear wheel drive
As built, affected vehicles have hardware consistent with a FGAWR of 1875kg but the IVL and IVD list the FGAWR of the vehicle as 2,100kg.
The order guide is unaffected and correctly states the vehicle FGAWR.

Based on Computer Aided Engineering (CAE) analysis, Ford concluded that the fatigue life of the front steering knuckles will be reduced if the front axle of an affected vehicle is loaded to the incorrectly listed 2,100kg FGAWR.
On August 16 2024, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concern and approved a field action.

events.quote: In June 2024, during inspection, an unusual noise coming from the engine drive belt was reported.
Cursory investigation identified that this might be linked to the installation of a second air conditioning compressor.
The issue was reported to Oliva Torras and analysis of the possible causes was initiated, both by Oliva Torras and Micro Bird.
Initially, the cause was identified as an increase of tension of the engine drive belt on the idler pulleys.

But after more tests, it was determined that the tensioner provided by Oliva Torras and that replaced the tensioner installed originally by GM, was not strong enough to correctly maintain the tension in the engine drive belt, allowing the drive belt to move on the pulleys and even become loose.
After identification of the defect and its safety risk, on September 16, 2024, it was decided to recall all the vehicles delivered with the identified second air conditioning compressor.
